title: Outer Horse Faster? v = ωr Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
In a ring game the kid at the end has to run while the kid at the centre just turns. Swing a cricket bat and the tip moves faster than the handle. On a merry-go-round, Diya's horse near the centre drifts while her friend's horse at the edge rushes, yet they go round together. How? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we link angular velocity and linear velocity.

On a live motion notebook a merry-go-round turns at 0.5 rad/s with omega drawn along the pole, the readout tracks the distance from the axis and the speed, and a graph shows the speed rising in a straight line as a marker walks out from the pole. A slow-mo replay freezes the outer horse to draw r from a point on the axis, theta and r perp, and shows why v = omega x r. We derive v = omega r perp = omega r sin theta step by step, see link by link why the outer horse is three times faster, compare the two horses side by side, and find the speed of the ground under our feet on the equator and in Bengaluru as the Earth turns. Then the exam trap (use r sin theta, not r), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
